name: Room-shape meter
summary: Hearing a room's volume from its mode count with a laptop's own speaker and mic. Stages 2, 5, 7 and 9 are built and run; the rest are on paper.

assumptions.assumption: walls are rigid enough that modes are Neumann modes
assumptions.how_checked: measured mode decay times are long (T60 above 0.3 s at low frequency)
assumptions.if_broken: the surface term changes sign or vanishes; V biased
assumptions.door: fit a wall-impedance term to the surface coefficient

assumptions.assumption: the source and the mic see every mode
assumptions.how_checked: corner to opposite-corner protocol; corners are antinodes of every mode
assumptions.if_broken: undercount; a mid-room mic misses about half
assumptions.door: average several mic positions instead of one corner

assumptions.how_checked: known-answer injection with two modes 1 Hz apart (R1)
assumptions.if_broken: undercount; this is the wall the matrix pencil attacks
assumptions.door: the matrix pencil resolves modes closer than a modal bandwidth

assumptions.assumption: mode spacing is Poisson (a box is integrable; Berry and Tabor 1977)
assumptions.how_checked: the corrected count against the twin's truth
assumptions.if_broken: the resolving correction is wrong for chaotic (irregular) rooms, whose spacings repel
assumptions.door: use a level-repulsion correction for irregular rooms

assumptions.assumption: the laptop records raw audio (no automatic gain, noise suppression or echo cancellation)
assumptions.how_checked: electrical or acoustic loopback reads a flat, linear response
assumptions.if_broken: the decay and the spectrum are rewritten by DSP; UNCAL
assumptions.door: an external audio interface with no processing

fixed_notes.c0: speed of sound in room air, m/s (about 20 C; from memory, moderate)
